key_insight: Low-frequency bow-shock unsteadiness in 3D shock/boundary-layer interaction is governed by a spanwise mass-balance mismatch between reattachment inflow and horseshoe-vortex outflow, which drives shock-foot flapping and asymmetry.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how protuberance shape and separation length control shock motion can help predict and mitigate unsteady loads, drag rise, and thermal/structural penalties in high-speed vehicle design.
method: Wind-tunnel tests at Mach 2.87 with protuberances of varying shape/size
Time-resolved surface pressure and schlieren imaging to measure shock/separation unsteadiness
Compressible adaptive DDES plus POD and two-point correlations for one cubical protuberance case
evidence_signal: Measurements showed low-frequency shock oscillations at St_δ≈0.01 and mid-frequency separated-region pressure oscillations at St_δ≈0.1, with POD revealing dominant anti-symmetric wall-pressure modes and spanwise phase lag.
watch_item: The mechanism is inferred from one detailed CFD case and selected diagnostics, so broader generalization across geometries and flow conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: On the governing mechanism of unsteadiness in bow shock-induced three-dimensional separation
